guide.title: Training guide
guide.rowHint: Set types, metrics, super-sets and blocks
guide.intro: What each thing you see while training means, explained for someone who doesn't live at the gym.

setTypes.title: Set types
setTypes.intro: Each set has a letter on its left: its type. Tap it to change it. Most sets are Normal; the other types say how that set is done.

WARMUP.body: Light sets to warm up before the real work. They don't count towards volume.

APPROACH.body: Sets that take you up to the working weight, a little at a time. They don't count towards volume either.

NORMAL.body: A regular working set: the weight and the reps the plan asks for.

ALL_OUT.body: Everything you have: as many reps, or as long, as you can hold with good form.

TO_FAILURE.body: Until you can't do one more good rep. Use it wisely, best on safe exercises.

DROP.body: When the set ends you lower the weight and keep going without resting, once or more. Each drop is a sub-set inside the set.

REST_PAUSE.body: Do the set, rest a few seconds (10–20) and carry on with the same weight. Each stretch is a sub-set.

CLUSTER.body: One set split into small chunks with very short rests between them, to move more weight or more reps.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.intro: Metrics are each exercise's columns: what you log for every set. Tap a column's name to see what it is.

plan.title: In a routine
plan.body: A routine says what to do: an exact value (8), a range (8–12), a maximum (<10) or a minimum (>5). Choose it with ⋯ › Change modes.

log.title: While training
log.body: You log what you did, one exact value per set. What the routine asks for — or what you did last time — shows in grey in each field: tick the set without typing and it keeps those values.

WEIGHT.name: Weight
WEIGHT.body: The load you move: the bar and its plates, the dumbbell, or what the machine shows.

REPS.name: Reps
REPS.body: How many times you do the full movement in the set.

RPE.name: RPE (rate of perceived exertion)
RPE.body: How hard the set was, from 1 to 10. A 10 means you couldn't do one more; an 8, that about two were left.
RPE.tip: It sets your effort without depending on the weight: on a bad day, the same RPE with fewer kilos.

RIR.name: RIR (reps in reserve)
RIR.body: How many more reps you could have done with good form. 0 is failure; 2, two to spare.

TIME.name: Time
TIME.body: How long the set lasts: a plank, a sprint, or the work of a Work/Rest block.

REST.name: Rest
REST.body: What the routine asks you to rest after the set. It's an instruction: shown, not logged.

DISTANCE.name: Distance
DISTANCE.body: How far you go: metres on a rower, kilometres on a run.

TEMPO.name: Tempo
TEMPO.body: The seconds of each phase of the movement: down, pause and up (3-1-1 is 3 down, 1 pause, 1 up). The routine sets it.

CALORIES.name: Calories
CALORIES.body: What the machine or the watch shows for that set.

CARDIO_ZONE.name: Cardio zone
CARDIO_ZONE.body: The intensity by heart rate, from zone 1 (very easy) to 5 (maximum). The routine sets it.

SPEED.name: Speed
SPEED.body: How fast you go: in km/h on a treadmill or a bike.

PACE.name: Pace
PACE.body: How long a kilometre (or a mile) takes you: 5:30 min/km.

REVOLUTIONS_PER_TIME.name: Revolutions / time
REVOLUTIONS_PER_TIME.body: The cadence: pedal (or rowing) strokes per minute.

CALORIES_PER_TIME.name: Calories / time
CALORIES_PER_TIME.body: The rate you burn at: calories per minute or hour, as some machines show it.

supersets.title: Super-sets
supersets.intro: A super-set joins two or more exercises done back to back, alternating, with the rest at the end of the round.

what.title: What for
what.body: It saves time and raises the intensity: while one muscle works, the other rests (bench press and row, for instance).

create.title: How to make one
create.body: On an exercise, ⋯ › Create super-set, and pick the other exercises of the same block it goes with.

sequence.title: The sequence
sequence.body: The sets show in the order they are done. Each exercise has a letter and each set its number: A1, B1, A2, B2… You can change the order, and which exercise does each set.

log.title: While training
log.body: Log and tick each set of the sequence, as on a regular exercise. The super-set is done when all of them are.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.intro: A block groups a routine's exercises under a name (Warm-up, Strength…). There are two kinds.

normal.title: Normal
normal.body: The usual table: you do each set at your own pace, log what you did and tick it.

workRest.title: Work/Rest
workRest.body: A timed circuit: every set has a work Time and a Rest (30 s and 15 s unless you say otherwise). The clock sets the pace, not you. You'll know it by the clock beside its name.

player.title: The clock
player.body: With Start, the screen counts 3-2-1 and runs the work and the rest with cues. You can pause, go back to the previous interval or skip to the next. When it closes, each set is ticked with the time you worked: the planned time if you reached the end, less if you skipped ahead.
